All Requirements for MBBS in Singapore

Understand the essential criteria and requirements

Ensure your eligibility for pursuing MBBS and starting your medical journey.

Eligibility Criteria to Apply for MBBS in Singapore 2025

To secure MBBS admission in Singapore, students must meet the following criteria:

  • Minimum 10+2 Qualification with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology.
  • High Academic Scores (at least 85% in PCB subjects).
  • BMAT Exam Score (required for some universities).
  • English Proficiency Test (IELTS/TOEFL for international students).
  • Strong Extracurricular & Leadership Skills (preferred by top universities).

Meeting these requirements enhances the chances of admission to top medical colleges in Singapore.

Intake for MBBS Study in Singapore

The MBBS admission process in Singapore is quite competitive, with a limited number of seats available for international students.

  • The primary intake of MBBS programs in Singapore is in August every year.
  • Application deadlines vary according to universities and are usually in January and March.
  • Those students who are interested in studying MBBS in Singapore as Indian students have to apply well in advance and meet eligibility criteria like academic merit and entrance exams like BMAT (Biomedical Admissions Test) for certain universities.

Since only a limited number of seats are available for overseas students in top medical colleges in Singapore, early registration makes a person more likely to be admitted. Scholarships and grants may be given at the point of intake as well.

Cost of MBBS in Singapore

SGD 150K - 250K
Average MBBS course fee For the complete course. Varies by university.

The cost of MBBS in Singapore varies with university and course. Fees in public universities are generally lower than in private universities. In addition to tuition fees, students will have to budget for laboratory fees and textbooks as well as medical insurance.

Living costs, including accommodation, food and transportation, will be between SGD 10,000 and SGD 20,000 a year. There are available scholarships that can help defray costs for deserving students. Medical colleges fees in singapore are affordable for Indian students, with reasonable living costs, attracting more and more Indian students to study MBBS in Singapore. Food and Accommodation for Indian Students

Diverse Options University hostels, private apartments, and shared accommodation.

Indian students studying MBBS in Singapore have a variety of accommodation options, including university hostels, private apartments, and shared accommodation. Accommodation on-campus ranges between SGD 400 and SGD 1,000 a month, and private accommodation ranges between SGD 800 and SGD 2,500 a month based on location and amenities.

For meals, there are a lot of food options to choose in Singapore, including Indian restaurants and vegetarian food. Home-cooking is a cheap alternative with groceries that range from SGD 200 to SGD 400 a month. With a multicultural population, Indian students can lead a convenient and inexpensive life while studying a medical course in Singapore.

Traveling Cost in Singapore

Public Transportation System Transport fares range between SGD 80 and SGD 120 a month.

Singapore possesses a well-planned and affordable public transportation system that makes it easy for students pursuing MBBS in Singapore to move around.

  • Unlimited rides on buses and on the MRT are available to students via EZ-Link or Singapore Tourist Pass.
  • A one-time ride on a bus or on an MRT ranges from SGD 0.80 to SGD 2.00.
  • Taxis and ride-hailing services like Grab are available but are more expensive.
  • Walking and cycling are used for short journeys in an attempt to save money.

Pathway Particulars

Duration of MBBS Course in Singapore

The duration of MBBS programs in Singapore is typically between 5 and 6 years and varies with the university and course structure. The National University of Singapore has a five-year MBBS course with a curriculum that includes pre-clinical education, clinical training, and internships. The first two years are spent on basic medical sciences and the next three years on clinical practice in hospitals and healthcare centers. A one-year specialist training internship is provided for selected students.

For foreign students like MBBS in Singapore for Indian students, successful program completion enables them to appear for medical licensure examinations and specialize further. With a well-designed and research-oriented system, Singapore provides a comprehensive medical education that is on a par with global healthcare standards.

Medium of Teaching in Singapore

The medium of instruction for MBBS in Singapore is English and is therefore a favorite destination among overseas students. English is employed by every medical college in Singapore as well as by the leading medical colleges in Singapore for lectures and clinical practice and exams. All language barriers are dispelled for Indian students and other foreign students who are studying MBBS in Singapore. Additionally, medical terminology and patient interaction are both in English as well, so learning is a smooth process.

Admission Procedure For Singapore MBBS College

A step-by-step roadmap to admission

  1. Fill out the admission form: Visit our official website https://www.rmcedu.com and complete the MBBS admission form with accurate details.
  2. Verification: The university will verify your application form, along with uploaded documents such as your passport, academic transcripts, and NEET scorecard, after you have submitted it.
  3. Screening: The university then undertakes a screening process in which the applicant must determine eligibility for admission to MBBS programs in Singapore.
  4. University-Wise Admission Shortlist: After the completion of the screening, the university will publish a shortlist of selected students for admission.
  5. Visa Process: After shortlisting, the student should apply for a student visa to the nearest Singapore Embassy or Consulate, attaching the confirmation of admission, passport, and other necessary documents.
  6. Physical Copy of Admission Letter: A hard copy of the admission letter will be sent by the university, which you will need to complete the visa process and enrollment.
  7. Fly to Singapore: Book your tickets and travel to Singapore to join your desired university.
  8. Complete enrollment once you reach there and start with your education.

Scholarships Offered for MBBS in Singapore

Studying MBBS in Singapore is expensive, but scholarships make it possible for international students and Indian students to pay tuition fees. Various government and university scholarships are provided on a merit and need basis.

  • Singapore International Graduate Award (SINGA): For excellent overseas students in medical research. Covers tuition, stipend, and grants.
  • ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship: Offered by NTU and NUS, includes living stipend and tuition fee for ASEAN students.
  • MOE Tuition Grant Scheme: Government tuition grants. Students are committed to serving in Singapore for at least three years after graduation.
  • Lee Kong Chian Scholarship: Provided at NUS for outstanding academic records. Covers tuition and a monthly stipend.

Campus Life for Medical Students in Singapore

Medical students in top medical colleges in Singapore have a well-balanced and rich college life.

  • Cutting-Edge Facilities: NUS and NTU possess well-equipped libraries, research labs, and student lounges.
  • Extracurriculars: Involved in medical clubs, cultural festivals, and leadership programs.
  • Hostel Accommodation: Provides a relaxed and convenient environment to stay with easy access to dining halls and recreational facilities.
  • Multicultural Environment: Makes MBBS in Singapore both educationally satisfying and socially engaging.

Career Opportunities after MBBS in Singapore

Career prospects after MBBS in Singapore have very good career opportunities in both clinical and research.

  • Work as a doctor in Singapore: Once a medical license is acquired, graduates are free to practice in public and private hospitals.
  • Specialize: They usually pursue postgraduate education in specialties like pediatrics, cardiology, or surgery.
  • Research and Academia: There are opportunities in medical research centers and universities.
  • Partner with International Orgs: With its globally recognized medical degree, physicians are free to practice overseas.
  • Join the Healthcare Management Sector: Hospital administrative roles, public health opportunities, and policy development.
